_meta.purpose: Curated pool of reliably-graspable YCB objects for the RoboMesh demo (experiments/robomesh/maniskill_robomesh_node.py). On every reset the node samples 6 entries at random from `objects` (rejection-sampled against min_separation_m) and spawns them via _spawn_objects().
_meta.seed_note: The apartment layout is a deterministic function of the episode seed: SceneManipulationEnv sets reconfiguration_freq=1 when num_envs==1 (mani_skill/envs/scenes/base_env.py:61-63), so EVERY reset() reconfigures and re-runs scene_builder.sample_build_config_idxs(), which is seeded by torch.manual_seed(episode_seed) (sapien_env.py:911-912). The node MUST build with seed 7.
_meta.apartment_note: md5 over every static actor name + world pose. Seeds 7, 8, 11, 12, 14 and 17 all produce this identical ReplicaCAD build config, so the grasp_task positions of those six benchmark scenes are interchangeable within it. Fetch spawns at (-1, 0, 0.02) in every build config, so there is no robot-spawn confound. The apartment itself contains no graspable objects; every object here comes from a benchmark grasp_task.
_meta.reliability_criterion: a run PASSES iff (success AND hold_success AND NOT collision_detected); tier = how many of the 5 independent benchmark runs passed; pool rule: tier >= 4/5

visibility_filter.rule: keep only tasks that are actually clickable in the tuned overview camera: in_frame AND unoccluded (ground-truth segmentation, each object rendered solo at its settled pose) AND clear of the two 300x225 HUD insets (the node drops clicks landing on an inset, _in_inset/resolve_click).
visibility_filter.result: 59 of the 66 tasks at >=4/5 are in-frame, unoccluded and clear of the insets under this pose. A solo-render pass removed the 7 tasks hidden by apartment geometry; the pool is only valid for THIS camera pose.

per_model_cap.rule: at most 4 entries per model_id so a random draw of 6 stays varied; within a model, 5/5 entries are kept in preference to 4/5

_meta.click_note: The node resolves a click by NEAREST projected object centre within 0.12*960 = 115 px (_resolve_click_scene), not by segmentation, so an object being only a few pixels wide does not make it unselectable -- the user clicks near it. 28 of the 58 entries render smaller than 60 px in this overview; they are kept deliberately for that reason. The closest co-spawnable projected centres are 19.4 px apart, so closely grouped objects require clicking near the desired centre.

entry_fields.model_id/position/orientation: exactly what _spawn_objects() needs; orientation is a SAPIEN quaternion (w,x,y,z), same order as grasp_benchmark.json
entry_fields.scene/task_id: provenance: the benchmark experiment this entry came from
entry_fields.tier/n_success/n_runs: reliability across the 5 independent benchmark runs
entry_fields.failure_reason: for 4/5 entries, why the single failed run failed; null for 5/5
entry_fields.uv_overview: pixel of the object's centre in the 960x720 tuned overview (audit aid)
entry_fields.visible_pixels: pixels the object occupies in that overview when rendered solo
entry_fields.bounding_radius_m: bounding-sphere radius about the spawn origin, from the real YCB collision.ply with ManiSkill's per-model scale

sampling.constraint: reject any draw in which two chosen entries are closer than min_separation_m (they would interpenetrate when co-spawned)

min_separation_derivation.why: Each benchmark task was run with ONE object in the scene, so their positions were never required to be mutually compatible. Co-spawning 6 of them CAN interpenetrate: the two closest entries in this pool are 0.034 m apart.
min_separation_derivation.method: Two objects can only interpenetrate if their centres are closer than r_i + r_j, where r is the bounding-sphere radius about the actor origin (= the spawn position). Because the sphere is centred on the origin, this bound holds for ANY spawn orientation. Radii were measured from the real YCB collision.ply with ManiSkill's own per-model scale (mani_skill/utils/building/actors/ycb.py:26-27).
min_separation_derivation.conclusion: min_separation_m = 0.3 exceeds the worst-case r_i+r_j of 0.266 m, so it PROVABLY prevents interpenetration for every pair in this pool (margin 0.034 m), while still leaving 93.5% of pairs legal and accepting a 6-draw on the first try 34% of the time.
